# pvecli backup prune

Prune backups by retention: preview from PVE first, then remove once confirmed.

Without any --keep-* option, the retention configured on the storage
applies. Protected backups are always kept.

```text
pvecli backup prune STORAGE [OPTIONS]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `STORAGE` | Backup storage to prune. |

## Options

| Option | Description |
|:--|:--|
| `--keep-last N` | Keep the N newest backups. |
| `--keep-hourly N` | Keep one backup per hour, N hours. |
| `--keep-daily N` | Keep one backup per day, N days. |
| `--keep-weekly N` | Keep one backup per week, N weeks. |
| `--keep-monthly N` | Keep one backup per month, N months. |
| `--keep-yearly N` | Keep one backup per year, N years. |
| `--vmid N` | Only the backups of this guest. |
| `--type VALUE` | Only qemu or lxc backups. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be removed, remove nothing. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skip confirmation. |
| `-p`, `--profile VALUE` | Profile to use. |

## Examples

```bash
pvecli backup prune local --keep-last 3 --keep-daily 7 --dry-run
pvecli backup prune pbs --keep-last 1 --vmid 100
```
